thread:
Anika Rao: Quick follow-up from the RFC review — folks raised concerns about where we apply RBAC for dashboard queries (early pushdown vs late merge). Wanted to collect a short plan and next steps.
Tom Barnes: +1. My gut is to prefer early pushdown for most filters to keep payload small, but caching becomes tricky if filters are user-specific.
Sanjay Patel: Right — pushdown helps latency and reduces compute, but if we push per-user predicates into the cache key we blow up cache cardinality.
Maya Li: Are we sure we need per-user pushdown? For many orgs we only have org-level roles. Maybe we can tier: org-level pushdown early, user-level authz applied after merge.
Anika Rao: That was an option in the RFC (tiered authz). Tradeoff list: 1) Early full pushdown = best latency, worst cache hit rate. 2) Early org-only pushdown = decent latency, reasonable cache. 3) Late authz = best cache reuse, worst p95 tail.
Tom Barnes: Also think about SLOs: dashboards have p50/p95 targets per customer tier. We could route critical customers to a path with stronger pushdown (dedicated cache namespace) and leave the rest on late authz.
Sanjay Patel: Implementation complexity matters. Inline authz in query adapters means touching many adapters (sql, elastic, custom) and tests for every one. Late merge centralizes authz code but needs re-eval of row-level decisions during the merge step.
Maya Li: Another dimension: telemetry. If we do early pushdown we lose visibility into which rows were filtered out later. For quality/monitoring we prefer a stage that can produce diff metrics (pre/post-authz counts).
Anika Rao: Good point — we should emit count metrics at adapter return and after authz merge either way. That helps detect regressions when we change pushdown strategy.
Tom Barnes: For caching we could use a hybrid cache key: [query-signature, org-version, authz-bucket]. Authz-bucket is coarse (e.g., public/org-only/private) to avoid per-user explosion.
Sanjay Patel: That aligns with the optimize team's suggestion of quantized authz layers. But we need a practical mapping from roles->buckets. Ops has to approve default mappings.
Maya Li: Rollout plan idea: start with org-only pushdown for all dashboards. Run a canary (5% of traffic) with full pushdown for customers flagged as "performance-safe". Collect cache hit rate, p95, and cost delta.
Anika Rao: +1. Metrics to collect: cache hit ratio, tokens processed (or rows scanned), p50/p95 latency, error rate, and pre/post authz row counts. Define dashboards for each.
Tom Barnes: FYI — inline code snippet for the proposed cache key change: 
```
cache_key = sha256(query_signature + ':' + org_id + ':' + authz_bucket)
```
Sanjay Patel: Operational concerns: when authz rules change we must invalidate affected cache buckets. We'll need an authz-version artifact that increments on policy changes.
Maya Li: Who owns the authz-version? Product or Security? Suggest Security owns the schema, ops owns the actual increment trigger via a small service.
Anika Rao: Action items: 1) Eng infra (Tom + Sanjay) to prototype authz-bucket mapping and cache-key change (ETA 2w). 2) DevEx (Maya) to add telemetry panels and pre/post authz counts. 3) Security to draft default bucket mapping doc. 4) Small canary plan doc (1 page) and rollout checklist.
Tom Barnes: I'll pick up the prototype and add unit tests for SQL + ES adapters.
Sanjay Patel: I'll sketch invalidation hooks and authz-version propagation in the cache service.
Maya Li: I'll create the telemetry panels and wire them into the console SLO dashboard (link to follow).
Anika Rao: ops-bot — please create a ticket for the canary run and assign tasks.
ops-bot: Created ticket INF-2026 (canary: dashboard authz pushdown experiment). Assignees: Tom Barnes, Sanjay Patel, Maya Li. Due: 2 weeks. :white_check_mark:
Tom Barnes: Quick note — we should include a regression test that measures cache hit drop when authz rules flip to a more granular level. Helps detect unintended cache fragmentation.
Sanjay Patel: Agreed. Also add a synthetic load test with mixed orgs (small/large) to estimate cost delta.
Maya Li: I'll schedule a short sync in 1 week to review the prototype metrics. 30min.
Anika Rao: Thanks all. I'll put the rollout checklist and the metric definitions into the RFC follow-up doc and ping the group when it's ready.
